title: api-config-runtime-arch-sketch-jamie-notes
content:
API config / runtime architecture sketch - notes to self

Context:
- Working through a lightweight config schema for runtime routing + caching + batching policies that product teams can pin per-route. Need something that maps cleanly to: Hosted API, Dedicated pools, Private (VPC) deployments.
- Goal: declarative, small set of knobs so non-runtimes engineers can tune cost vs latency without breaking things.

Problem statement:
- Users want to set per-route SLOs (p50/p99 latency targets), cost preference (latency-first | cost-first | balanced), and hints for batching/kv-cache. Runtime needs to translate into: pool selection (dedicated vs shared), batch size limits, kv-cache TTL/prefixing, and fallback model variants.

Non-goals (for MVP):
- Full feature-flag rollout semantics (we should integrate with rollouts later)
- Per-customer hardware pinning in this config (handled by infra)

Constraints:
- Latency SLO must be enforceable at p99 under normal load. Runtime can override aggressive batching if SLO violated.
- Default policy should be safe for multi-tenant shared pools.
- Config must be serializable to JSON/YAML and small (< 2KB) per-route.

Rough config schema (YAML-ish sketch):

route: /chat/completion
model: gpt-medium-v1
version: pinned-2025-01-15
policy:
  slo_ms:
    p50: 60
    p99: 300
  preference: latency-first  # values: latency-first | cost-first | balanced
  pool_selector:
    mode: auto  # auto | dedicated | private
    min_qps: 10
  batching:
    enable: true
    max_batch_size: 64
    max_wait_ms: 12
    batch_by: session_id  # hints for grouping; optional
  kv_cache:
    enable: true
    prefix: route_prefix  # runtime will hash + model+version
    ttl_seconds: 300
  fallbacks:
    - model: gpt-small-quantized
      reason: cost-fallback
      max_latency_ms: 800

Notes on fields:
- pool_selector.mode=auto -> runtime decides based on current capacity, cost preference, and region. If preference=latency-first, prefer dedicated when available.
- batching.max_wait_ms is a soft-signal; runtime can reduce wait if p99 trending high.
- kv_cache.prefix should combine route, model, and customer id when present (privacy). For private deployments, default TTL can be longer.

Example API surface (for product teams):
POST /v1/routes/:route_id/config -> returns current active config
PUT /v1/routes/:route_id/config -> upsert user config (RBAC + validation)
GET /v1/routes/:route_id/status -> real-time rollout + backing pool info

Runtime translation rules (rough):
- If preference == cost-first AND traffic < min_qps -> route to shared pooled nodes + enable aggressive kv-cache + bump max_batch_size
- If slo_ms.p99 <= 200 -> set batch.max_wait_ms <= 8 and cap max_batch_size to 16 to prioritize latency
- If pool_selector.mode == dedicated -> attempt to bind to dedicated pool; if capacity not available, use canary fallback for 5 minutes then escalate to infra/team alert

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we expose "burst_capacity" as a top-level knob or keep it infra-only? (leaning infra-only with product-visible slider)
- How to represent multi-model fallback chain (priority, cost thresholds)? Simple list vs tree?
- Validation rules: syntactic checks + safety checks (e.g., p99 < p50 not allowed). Where to enforce? API layer vs control plane?
- Backwards compatibility: need migration for existing routes. Add a versioned schema field.

Operational considerations:
- Add telemetry: decisions emitted per-request (why batching chosen, cache hit/miss, pool decision) to console traces (low-sample for perf).
- Config audit trail (who changed, when) + automatic lint: warn if cost-first + p99 < 100ms (likely impossible).

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- Iterate this sketch with Casey (batching knobs) and Samir (pool selection signals) -- schedule 30m sync
- Prototype server-side validator + sample UI for route config in console (low-fi mock)
- Link to INF-324 (routing policy epic) and PR #789 for runtime kernel changes that affect batching timing

Quick links and references:
- INF-324 (routing & policy epic): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-324
- PR that changed batch timing heuristics: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789
- Slack thread: #runtime-batching (see thread id above)

Random notes to self:
- Keep schema minimal at first; product teams often confuse too many knobs -> ship defaults that work for 90% traffic.
- Add examples in docs for "Chat bot with low latency" vs "Batch embeddings for nightly job".

-- Jamie
